sections.title: Executive investment summary: a niche belting maker wrapped around a promoter-linked treasury book

blocks.text: International Conveyors Ltd (ICL) makes solid-woven, PVC-impregnated, fire-retardant anti-static (FRAS) conveyor belting, used mainly in underground coal and potash mines [F] (AR2025 p.37). It has two plants, at Aurangabad (Maharashtra, 700,000 m/yr installed) and Falta SEZ (West Bengal, 425,000 m/yr) [F] (AR2025 p.37). FY25 production was 304,359 metres [F] (AR2025 p.37). It also trades Mato fasteners and steel-cord belting, sells power from five windmills, and runs a treasury segment that invests in listed equities and lends inter-corporate deposits [F] (AR2025 p.40-41). The belting business makes money on engineered, approval-gated belts sold mostly for export, largely FOB, under contracts that management says carry index-linked price-variation clauses [MC] (CALL Jun 2022).

blocks.caption: Revenue and profit mix, FY25 standalone (Rs crore)

items: End markets: domestic belting went about 85% to coal in FY24 and about 93% in FY25 [F] (PPT Jun 2025). Exports went mainly to potash, roughly 79-82% of export revenue by industry in the chart pair [F] (PPT Jun 2025). The chart does not say clearly which year each pie belongs to, so the split by year is our reading [AI].

Geography: consolidated FY25 product sales were Rs 102.0 cr export and Rs 49.2 cr domestic, so 67% export [F] (AR2025 p.195) [E]. CARE puts exports at about 63% of standalone belt sales in FY26, against 65% in FY25 [F] (RATING).
Within exports, Canada was 70.2% and 82.3% in the two years shown, with USA and the rest of the world making up the remainder [F] (PPT Jun 2025). We read the higher figure as FY25 [AI].

Customers: in FY25 the top five customers took about 81% of standalone revenue (74% in FY24), and the top six took 83% of consolidated revenue [F] (AR2025 p.123, p.195). The named anchor is Viacore Solutions Inc, whose exclusive supply agreement for Nutrien was renewed for five years in January 2025. In India, Coal India and its subsidiaries are the major client [F] (RATING).

blocks.text: Listing status: ICL is a long-listed company on BSE (scrip 509709) and NSE (INTLCONV), incorporated in 1973 [F] (AR2025 p.1; SCREENER). No prospectus or recent offer document was available. The evidence base is one annual report (FY25), one earnings-call transcript from June 2022, one investor presentation (June 2025), a CARE rating note (July 2026), exchange announcements, and screener statements up to the June 2026 quarter [F] (NUMBERS). **No Q1 FY27 earnings call or presentation was in the evidence, and there was no call transcript after June 2022**, so management commentary for the current year is thin [AI].

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. Reported profit is mostly market marks, not belting. Other income was 87% of PBT in FY24, 90.5% in FY25 and 66% in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). In Q1 FY27 other income was Rs 147 cr against EBITDA of Rs 7 cr [F] (NUMBERS). The FY26 PBT of Rs 88.5 cr included Rs 45.3 cr of fair-value gains on equities [F] (RATING).

2. Cash is lent to the promoter group. At Mar-2025 all Rs 122.2 cr of loans outstanding were to promoters or related parties, unsecured and repayable on demand [F] (AR2025 p.72, p.102). The loan to I G E (India), the holding company, peaked at Rs 149.9 cr during FY25 [F] (AR2025 p.102). Group exposure was Rs 149.9 cr at Mar-2026, about 35% of tangible net worth [F] (RATING).

3. The promoter group is leveraging up to delist Elpro International. IGE and Zenox have raised Rs 420 cr of five-year loans, and group LAS debt was about Rs 784 cr against a Rs 2,396 cr investment book at Mar-2026 [F] (RATING). A non-disposal undertaking covers 50.69% of ICL's shares [F] (RATING). The risk is that ICL's balance sheet is pulled further into funding the group [AI].

4. The treasury book is itself leveraged and pledged. ICL drew Rs 57.1 cr of LAS against a Rs 220 cr sanction and has pledged equities worth Rs 231.8 cr [F] (RATING). In FY25 it booked a Rs 0.49 cr F&O trading loss [F] (AR2025 p.112), although its risk note says derivatives are used exclusively for hedging [F] (AR2025 p.131).

5. Concentration is extreme and rising. The top five customers were 81% of standalone revenue in FY25, up from 74% [F] (AR2025 p.123). One distributor, Viacore, serves Nutrien [F] (RATING), and Canada was 70-82% of exports [F] (PPT Jun 2025).

6. The operating business has barely grown. The 3-year sales CAGR is -0.3% [F] (NUMBERS). Sales fell 38% in FY24 [F] (NUMBERS), 46% of FY26 sales came in Q4 [E] (NUMBERS), and Q1 FY27 sales were flat year on year at Rs 35 cr [F] (NUMBERS).

7. The overseas subsidiaries destroy value. International Conveyors America lost Rs 2.7 cr in FY25 on Rs 16.3 cr of turnover and has negative equity. Conveyor Holdings Pte was impaired by Rs 16.6 cr [F] (AR2025 p.137, p.78).

8. Governance is in transition. The founder-MD died on 24-Nov-2024 and the Executive Director resigned on 13-Nov-2024 [F] (AR2025 p.22-23). The new CMD has a financial-services background [F] (PPT Jun 2025). Founder-MD pay of Rs 4.85 cr in FY24 [F] (AR2025 p.26) equalled about 23% of consolidated EBITDA [E] (NUMBERS).

9. On operating cash flows alone the valuation is unsupported. Our DCF gives Rs 5.4 (bear), Rs 16.3 (base) and Rs 23.4 (bull) per share against a price of Rs 80, and the reverse DCF implies 106.8% annual sales growth [F] (NUMBERS). The model's treatment of the investment book explains much of this gap (see valuation) [AI].

10. Unexplained FY26 revenue. CARE's standalone FY26 total operating income of Rs 203.65 cr includes Rs 163.93 cr of belt sales [F] (RATING). That leaves about Rs 39.7 cr of non-belt revenue, against about Rs 9.1 cr in FY25 [E] (RATING). What makes up the difference is not disclosed [AI].

subsections.title: Key debates: what the market may be getting wrong

items: Holding-company discount or governance trap? Market cap of Rs 510 cr against Rs 328 cr of investments and about Rs 140 cr of group loans [F] (NUMBERS; RATING) looks like a discounted holdco. But the loans are on-demand money to promoter entities that are themselves raising leverage [F] (RATING). A discount may be rational [AI].

Is the 19-20% EBITDA margin structural? FY26 OPM was 19% and Q1 FY27 20% [F] (NUMBERS). CARE attributes this to better absorption of fixed overheads [F] (RATING). Margins were 14-16% in FY23-FY25 and fell to 1.5% in the Dec-2024 quarter [F] (NUMBERS). We see the level as volume-dependent, not proven structural [AI].

The 'Coal India proxy' framing (our earlier dashboard notes) is wrong on mix: exports are 63-67% of sales and potash for Canada dominates [F] (RATING; PPT Jun 2025) [AI] (BOARD). The main risk is a single Canadian potash chain, not the Coal India cycle [AI].

The headline P/E of 3.8x [F] (NUMBERS) reflects Q1 FY27 mark-to-market gains. The belting business earned PBT of about Rs 30 cr in FY26 (EBITDA 40 less depreciation 2 less interest 8) [E] (NUMBERS), so reported P/E overstates cheapness, in both directions depending on equity markets [AI].

The weak-cash-conversion red flag partly misleads the other way. Cash from operations excludes investment gains by construction, and CFO/EBITDA was 0.88x in FY26 [E] (NUMBERS). The operating business converts reasonably [AI].

blocks.text: Our view [AI]: ICL is best analysed as three pieces. The first is a small, approval-protected export belting business with about Rs 30-40 cr of EBITDA and one dominant Canadian channel. The second is a roughly Rs 330 cr marked-to-market equity book. The third is roughly Rs 140-150 cr of on-demand loans to promoter entities that are simultaneously borrowing about Rs 420 cr to take Elpro private [F] (NUMBERS; RATING). The operating DCF says the belt business alone does not support the price [F] (NUMBERS). The treasury book arguably does, but only if minority holders can rely on it being there. The variant view is that **the investment case turns on capital allocation and related-party discipline, not on belting demand**. The next few disclosures on group exposure and the Elpro delisting matter more than the next quarter's belt sales [AI].
Earnings are market-driven. Q2 FY26 PAT was -Rs 17 cr on other income of -Rs 32 cr, and Q1 FY27 PAT was Rs 120 cr on other income of +Rs 147 cr [F] (NUMBERS). Do not annualise either.

Old evidence about the belting business, such as the 2022 call, says little about how the current leadership will allocate capital [AI].

sections.title: Business model: vertically integrated weaving and PVC impregnation

items: 1. Inputs: polyester, cotton and spun yarn plus PVC resin, phosphate plasticiser and other chemicals [F] (AR2025 p.111). About half are imported (Europe, China, Thailand, Norway), per management in 2022 [MC] (CALL Jun 2022).
2. Yarn preparation: twisting and doubling machines handle up to 20 tonnes of yarn at a time [MC] (AR2025 p.37).
3. Beaming: a 2,400 mm beam-width machine, described as one of the widest in the world [MC] (AR2025 p.37).
4. Weaving: solid-woven carcass on shuttle looms with up to 2,100 mm reed space [MC] (PPT Jun 2025).
5. Impregnation and coating: a vacuum impregnation tower and an integrated coating plant apply the PVC; quartz infra-red curing follows [MC] (PPT Jun 2025).
6. Testing: in a NABL-accredited laboratory (drum friction, flame, fire propagation and electrical resistance tests) [MC] (PPT Jun 2025).
7. Approval and design support: country and customer approvals; in-house system design using Sidewinder software [MC] (PPT Jun 2025; AR2025 p.38).

8. Delivery: mostly FOB Indian port, with some DDP [MC] (CALL Jun 2022). Sales go through subsidiaries in the US and Australia and an exclusive distributor (Viacore) for Nutrien [F] (AR2025 p.126; RATING).

blocks.text: The value sits in approvals and fire-safety performance, not in the raw weaving [AI]. The gross margin proxy moved between 37% and 53% over FY20-FY25 [E] (PPT Jun 2025). The conveyor belting segment's PBIT margin was about 22% in FY24 and FY25 (Rs 28.7 cr on Rs 129.6 cr; Rs 29.5 cr on Rs 132.7 cr) [E] (AR2025 p.122). That is consistent with some pricing power in a niche [AI]. Management claims that price-variation clauses pass raw-material costs through every six months [MC] (CALL Jun 2022). CARE instead says ICL mainly bids for short-term fixed-price orders based on inventory in hand [F] (RATING). The two descriptions are not reconciled.

Capital intensity is very low. Net fixed assets are Rs 15 cr [F] (NUMBERS) against gross fixed assets of Rs 30.4 cr (FY25 standalone) [F] (AR2025 p.210). Capex has been Rs 0-4 cr a year except FY19 (Rs 13 cr) [F] (NUMBERS). Only Rs 0.22 cr of capital commitments were outstanding at Mar-2025 [F] (AR2025 p.114). The model outsources little manufacturing and some distribution [AI]. Working capital, not fixed capital, absorbs cash, and the treasury book absorbs most of the equity [AI].

sections.title: Segments: belting drives revenue, treasury drives profit

blocks.text: Segment margins are disclosed as segment results. Standalone belting PBIT was Rs 28.69 cr in FY24 and Rs 29.50 cr in FY25; consolidated belting was Rs 28.45 cr and Rs 27.73 cr [F] (AR2025 p.122, p.193). The consolidated figure is below standalone because the subsidiaries lose money [AI]. Treasury PBT was Rs 56.6 cr in FY24 and Rs 78.6 cr in FY25 after a Rs 16.6 cr impairment, making it 78% of standalone PBT [F] (AR2025 p.41).

items: Belting FY24 fall: management said Canadian demand would stay sluggish because of reduced international potash offtake [MC] (PPT Jun 2025). Our read [AI]: the Viacore renewal fell due in Sep-2024 and was signed only in Jan-2025 [F] (RATING). Exports jumped 142% year on year in Q4 FY25 to Rs 45.5 cr [F] (PPT Jun 2025), which suggests contract timing drove FY24-FY25 as much as end demand did.
Belting FY26 rise: CARE cites the Viacore renewal and improved Coal India demand [F] (RATING). Our read [AI]: Q4 FY26 sales of Rs 97 cr [F] (NUMBERS) point to lumpy shipments, not a smooth step-up.

Trading: management blames a lack of export orders [MC] (AR2025 p.41), yet the MD&A says it expects substantial growth in Mato products [MC] (AR2025 p.38). The two statements sit uneasily together [AI].
Wind: management blames low wind velocity [MC] (AR2025 p.41). The Chitradurga turbine generated 0 kWh in FY25 [F] (AR2025 p.33).
Treasury: gains of Rs 76.0 cr from fair-valuing current investments in FY25 [F] (AR2025 p.110) track equity markets, not company operations [AI].

blocks.text: Order-driven vs organic [AI]: export belting is contract- and order-driven, with a Rs 68.3 cr export order book [F] (RATING). Domestic coal belting is tender-driven [MC] (CALL Jun 2022). Trading and wind are organic but immaterial. Treasury is market-driven.

blocks.text: About half of FY26's Rs 61 cr revenue increase is not explained by belt sales. CARE's standalone total operating income (Rs 203.65 cr) exceeds its belt sales (Rs 163.93 cr) by about Rs 39.7 cr [F] (RATING), against a non-belt run-rate of about Rs 9 cr in FY25 [F] (AR2025 p.122). Until the FY26 annual report is available, treat this as unexplained [AI].

Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 35 cr, flat year on year, with EBITDA of Rs 7 cr at a 20% OPM [F] (NUMBERS). The order book was Rs 76.01 cr at 30-Apr-2026 (Rs 68.32 cr export, mainly Canada; Rs 7.69 cr domestic), against about Rs 62 cr a year earlier [F] (RATING). No revenue guidance for FY27 was found in the documents [F] (RATING; PPT Jun 2025). CARE only says growth is expected to be supported by execution of the order book and steady export demand [F] (RATING). We do not infer any guidance [AI].

blocks.text: Longer history: by FY13, 70% of sales were international [MC] (PPT Jun 2025), and management cited about 80% exports in 2022 [MC] (CALL Jun 2022). The FY26 share of 63% [F] (RATING) is lower than that. Our read [AI]: the drop comes from domestic Coal India demand recovering, not from a strategy to de-emphasise exports. Management's stated strategy is still to grow exports into Europe, Australia, South Africa and Central Asia [MC] (PPT Jun 2025).

items: Currency: foreign-exchange earnings were Rs 94.8 cr in FY25 against CIF imports of Rs 28.9 cr [F] (AR2025 p.33), so ICL is a net USD earner [AI]. As a policy it does not hedge [F] (RATING). FX gains were Rs 2.31 cr in FY26 and Rs 1.18 cr in FY25 [F] (RATING).

Tariffs and trade policy: the documents contain no discussion of US or Canadian tariffs on Indian belting and no dated trade-policy events. The MD&A lists trade wars only as a generic risk [MC] (AR2025 p.40). The US was roughly 9-21% of exports [F] (PPT Jun 2025). Tariff exposure is therefore unquantified, which is a disclosure gap [AI].
Management said in 2025 that it would evaluate Europe 'including Russia and Belarus' [MC] (PPT Jun 2025). That carries sanctions risk not discussed in the documents [AI].

Location: there are two plants, but approvals are granted per geography per plant [MC] (PPT Jun 2025). The Falta SEZ plant was built to serve international markets [MC] (PPT Jun 2025). A disruption at the approved plant for a given market could halt that market, but which plant holds which approval is not disclosed [AI].

sections.title: Working capital: the operating cycle is modest, the headline metric is not

subsections.title: Headline days and why they mislead

blocks.text: Our statements data flag working-capital days of 646 in FY26, up from a 76-day average [F] (NUMBERS). This measure appears to include non-operating current assets such as group loans and receivables from investment sales, which were Rs 12.3 cr at Mar-2025 [F] (AR2025 p.102) [AI]. The operating cash conversion cycle was 42 days in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS), and CARE's operating cycle was 37 days [F] (RATING). Read alone, the headline number overstates operating working-capital stress [AI].

Receivables were 79% from overseas customers at Mar-2025 (standalone) [E] (AR2025 p.123). Standalone receivables overdue by more than one year were Rs 0.62 cr, including Rs 0.14 cr of credit-impaired debts [F] (AR2025 p.101).

subsections.title: Drivers, cash consequence and bank limits

items: Management's explanation: inventory is held because of import lead times and customer inspections, and the holding period depends on the expected raw-material price trend [F] (RATING). In 2022 management cited 'efficiency in working capital management', claiming -6 working-capital days for FY22 [MC] (CALL Jun 2022).
Evidence: inventory days swung from 71 to 161 and back to 84 between FY23 and FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). Our read is that swings follow export shipment timing more than policy [AI].
Cash consequence: the FY24 build absorbed cash (CFO Rs 12 cr) and the FY25 release helped (inventory down by Rs 9.5 cr) [F] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.149).

Bank limits: cash credit Rs 22 cr, EPC/PSC Rs 25 cr, BG/LC Rs 25 cr. Average fund-based utilisation was about 47% over the 12 months to Apr-2026 [F] (RATING). No covenants apply to the rated facilities [F] (RATING). Quarterly stock statements agreed with the books [F] (AR2025 p.71).

sections.title: Balance-sheet quality: liquid, but a quarter of assets are promoter loans

items: Borrowings were Rs 73 cr at Mar-2026 [F] (NUMBERS): LAS Rs 57.08 cr (sanction Rs 220 cr) and an ECGS term loan of Rs 9.5 cr, with the rest working capital [F] (RATING).
Contingent liabilities at Mar-2025: income-tax demand of Rs 0.73 cr, and bank guarantees of Rs 9.93 cr (up from Rs 6.87 cr) [F] (AR2025 p.114).
Pledges: listed equities worth Rs 231.81 cr are pledged for the LAS [F] (RATING). Fixed deposits are pledged as margin for letters of credit and bank guarantees [F] (AR2025 p.99, p.102).

The working-capital facilities are also backed by a personal guarantee from a director [F] (AR2025 p.108). The guarantor was the late MD per the related-party note [F] (AR2025 p.127). Who guarantees them now is not disclosed [AI].

Related-party leases: none separately disclosed. Small purchases of services from Elpro (Rs 0.29 cr) and rent received from R.C.A. (Rs 0.003 cr) appear in FY25 related-party transactions [F] (AR2025 p.126).

blocks.text: Assessment [AI]: the balance sheet is liquid and lightly geared, but its quality depends on two things outside the belting business: equity-market levels, and the willingness and ability of promoter entities, which are themselves raising Rs 420 cr for the Elpro delisting [F] (RATING), to repay on-demand loans.

items: Auditor: G P Agrawal & Co (FRN 302082E), partner Sunita Kedia. Re-appointed in 2022 for five years to the 54th AGM (2027) [F] (AR2025 p.24-25, p.70).

FY25 opinions on the standalone and consolidated accounts are unmodified, with no qualification, reservation or adverse remark [F] (AR2025 p.25). We found no emphasis-of-matter paragraph in the FY25 reports [F] (AR2025 p.67-70, p.139).
Key Audit Matter: valuation of investments, 61% of standalone and 59% of consolidated total assets [F] (AR2025 p.67, p.139).
Audit trail: the plant's accounting software does not capture the nature of changes made. The auditor therefore qualified its books-of-account statement under Rule 11(g) [F] (AR2025 p.69-70).

CARO: all Rs 122.18 cr of loans outstanding were to promoters or related parties and repayable on demand. One Rs 1.31 cr loan to another company is overdue and fully provided [F] (AR2025 p.71-72). Disputed income tax of Rs 5.78 lakh is outstanding [F] (AR2025 p.72). There were no defaults, no fraud and no whistle-blower complaints [F] (AR2025 p.73).
The statutory audit fee was Rs 2.75 lakh [F] (AR2025 p.112). That is very low for a Rs 500 cr balance sheet with a KAM on investments [AI].

Exceptional item: a Rs 16.6 cr impairment of Conveyor Holdings Pte in the standalone accounts, with no counterpart in the consolidated P&L [F] (AR2025 p.78, p.148). Consolidated PAT therefore exceeds standalone PAT [AI].
Segment policy changed in FY24, when investments became a reportable segment [F] (AR2025 p.121).
Restatements: only routine regrouping of prior-year figures [F] (AR2025 p.136). No common-control transactions are disclosed.

The documents do not cover: the FY26 annual report and audit report, the Q1 FY27 limited review, subsidiary audit reports, internal-audit findings, or FY26 CARO. This is a material gap for a company whose FY26 revenue bridge is partly unexplained [AI].

blocks.text: Overall assessment [AI]: the opinion is clean and the accounting is mechanically straightforward, since mark-to-market gains are recognised through P&L under FVTPL. The weaknesses are the audit-trail gap, the cost-records contradiction, derivative trading that contradicts the stated policy, and a very small audit fee relative to the complexity of the investments. Accounting quality is adequate; disclosure quality is weak.

blocks.text: Key forensic conclusion [AI]: the 106.8% implied growth is an artefact, not a market expectation. The reverse DCF asks the belting business to justify an EV of Rs 583 cr, which embeds the market's valuation of a Rs 328 cr equity portfolio and about Rs 140 cr of related-party loans [F] (NUMBERS; RATING). The honest reading is that the market pays about Rs 510 cr for three things: a belting business the DCF values at Rs 34-149 cr of equity, a marked-to-market portfolio, and promoter-group receivables. The price therefore sits at a discount or premium to those assets depending on how much one trusts the receivables and the portfolio's durability [AI].

Strongest counter-argument [AI]: minorities have no claim on the treasury book except through dividends (payout 5% [F] (NUMBERS)) or a buyback. Part of the portfolio is pledged [F] (RATING), marks can reverse (Q2 FY26 other income -Rs 32 cr [F] (NUMBERS)), and the on-demand loans go to entities that are borrowing Rs 420 cr for the Elpro delisting [F] (RATING). summary.one_line: International Conveyors is a small, approval-protected PVC mining-belt exporter with 19-20% operating margins, wrapped around a Rs 328 cr marked-to-market equity book and about Rs 140 cr of on-demand loans to a promoter group that is levering up to delist Elpro. The Rs 80 price is far above the operating DCF (Rs 5.4-23.4 per share), and whether it is justified depends on governance and capital allocation, not on belting growth.
bull_points: [F] Investments of Rs 328 cr at Mar-2026 equal about 64% of the Rs 510 cr market cap [E], and the operating DCF gives them no value (NUMBERS).
[F] Viacore Solutions' exclusive agreement to supply Nutrien was renewed for five years in Jan-2025; the export order book was Rs 68.32 cr of Rs 76.01 cr at 30-Apr-2026 (RATING).
[F] Operating margin rose to 19% in FY26 and 20% in Q1 FY27 from 14% in FY25, on better absorption of fixed costs (NUMBERS; RATING).
[F] Country-level mine-safety approvals (DGMS, MSHA, CSA, TestSafe, SANS) form a slow-to-replicate barrier (PPT Jun 2025).
[E] FY25 production of 304,359 m against 1.125 mn m installed implies about 27% utilisation, leaving capex-free volume headroom (AR2025 p.37).
bear_points: [F] All Rs 122.2 cr of loans at Mar-2025 were to promoters or related parties, unsecured and on demand; group exposure was Rs 149.92 cr (about 35% of TNW) at Mar-2026 (AR2025 p.72; RATING).
[F] The promoter group raised Rs 420 cr to delist Elpro, carries about Rs 784 cr of group LAS debt, and has given a non-disposal undertaking on 50.69% of ICL (RATING).
[F] Other income was 66-90.5% of PBT in FY24-FY26, and Rs 147 cr against Rs 7 cr of EBITDA in Q1 FY27; reported PAT swings with equity markets (NUMBERS).
[F] Top-five customers were 81% of standalone revenue in FY25, up from 74%, and Canada was 70-82% of exports (AR2025 p.123; PPT Jun 2025).
[F] The 3-year sales CAGR is -0.3%, and the DCF values the operating business at Rs 5.4 / 16.3 / 23.4 per share against a price of Rs 80 (NUMBERS).
